surface_forms: une femme que tu ne veux pas connaître

appraisal_events.evidence: « une femme que tu ne veux pas connaître [...] je ne l'aurai jamais chez moi plus tard [...] C'est la femme de Swann » ; « comme je la connais de vue je me lèverai à temps » ; « Je n'en doute pas, mais je n'éprouve aucun besoin de m'en assurer par moi-même ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Odette is staged as the woman one arranges not to meet: Mme de Villeparisis apologizes in advance for the single exception, and the duchesse plans her exit and refuses even Mme de Marsantes' vouching for her. The exclusion is a coordinated act of the salon, delivered as an unremarkable social fact.

appraisal_events.evidence: « la duchesse de Guermantes, si amie de Swann, eût, au contraire, toujours résisté au désir qu'il ne lui avait pas caché de lui présenter sa femme [...] elle jugeait qu'elle « n'avait pas » à faire telle ou telle chose, et imposait avec despotisme ce qu'avait décidé son « libre arbitre » mondain, fort arbitraire ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator undercuts the refusal he has just reported: the duchesse's exclusion is not principle but caprice, and the scare-quoted « libre arbitre » plus « fort arbitraire » reframes her sovereignty as despotic whim exercised against a man she calls a friend.

status_effects.explanation: She is explicitly barred from the valued social space: admitted once as a nuisance to be forewarned about, never to be received again, and avoided in person by the duchesse.
She holds the floor and closes the exchange with an unanswerable epigram, disposing of Mme de Marsantes' defense without conceding anything.
The narrator's aside makes her exclusion look arbitrary and despotic, and disloyal toward Swann, so her local standing with the reader falls even as her salon authority is confirmed.

ambiguities: Odette's local movement is genuinely double: her opportunistic nationalism and antisemitism (modelled on Mme Verdurin) do win her entry into fashionable anti-Dreyfusard leagues and aristocratic connections, a real social gain, yet the scene itself is organized around her exclusion by the Guermantes. The exclusion is treated here as dominant because it is what the passage stages, while the climb is reported in narratorial summary and is itself ironized (she disavows her husband's cause and his origins to obtain it).

The narrator's account of the duchesse's caprice is deferred (« on verra plus tard ») and framed as explanation rather than verdict, so it can be read as neutral characterization; the loaded terms « despotisme » and « fort arbitraire », with « libre arbitre » in scare quotes, are taken here as tipping it into ironized diminishment.
